---
title: "World Toilet Day: Complete plumbing access in the United States"
author: "Jennifer Peebles, The Atlanta Journal-Constitution"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
params:
  data_year: 2024
  output_root: "output"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center"
)

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

data_path <- file.path(params$output_root, "data")
graphics_path <- file.path(params$output_root, "graphics")

read_plumbing_output <- function(geography) {
  readr::read_csv(
    file.path(
      data_path,
      paste0("b25047_", geography, "_", params$data_year, ".csv")
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )
}

us <- read_plumbing_output("us")
states <- read_plumbing_output("state")
counties <- read_plumbing_output("county")
places <- read_plumbing_output("place")
qa <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(data_path, "qa_summary.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## National overview

The Census Bureau estimates that `r scales::comma(us$lacking)` housing
housing units lacked complete plumbing facilities in the United States in the
`r params$data_year - 4`–`r params$data_year` American Community Survey
five-year period. That represents `r scales::percent(us$pct_lacking,
accuracy = 0.1)` of housing units, with a 90% confidence interval from
`r scales::percent(us$pct_lacking_ci_low, accuracy = 0.1)` to
`r scales::percent(us$pct_lacking_ci_high, accuracy = 0.1)`.

## State pattern

```{r state-map, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(
  file.path(
    graphics_path,
    paste0("map_states_pct_lacking_", params$data_year, ".jpg")
  )
)
```

```{r state-table}
states %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_lacking)) %>%
  select(
    State = name_clean,
    `Housing units lacking complete plumbing` = lacking,
    `Percent lacking` = pct_lacking,
    `90% MOE` = pct_lacking_moe,
    Reliability = pct_lacking_reliability
  ) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(
    `Housing units lacking complete plumbing` =
      scales::comma(`Housing units lacking complete plumbing`),
    `Percent lacking` = scales::percent(
      `Percent lacking`,
      accuracy = 0.1
    ),
    `90% MOE` = scales::percent(`90% MOE`, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "States with the largest estimated shares lacking complete plumbing"
  )
```

## Reliability and QA

ACS figures are estimates. The Census Bureau publishes a 90% margin of error
for each estimate. This project also calculates confidence bounds,
zero-overlap flags and coefficients of variation.

```{r qa-table}
qa %>%
  select(
    Geography = geography,
    Rows = rows,
    `CI overlaps zero: percent lacking` =
      pct_lacking_ci_overlaps_zero,
    `Low reliability: percent lacking` =
      pct_lacking_low_reliability,
    `Not classifiable: percent lacking` =
      pct_lacking_not_classifiable
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Quality-assurance summary")
```

## Disease context

Typhoid, paratyphoid and cholera once killed thousands of Americans at a time.
Modern public water and sanitation systems, vaccination and medical treatment
helped make these diseases rare in the United States.

The CDC surveillance figures below are descriptive historical context only.
They are not joined to or correlated with the ACS plumbing data. Most recent
U.S. typhoid and cholera cases are associated with international travel.

```{r cdc-context, out.width="100%"}
cdc_graphic <- file.path(
  graphics_path,
  "cdc_typhoid_cholera_context.jpg"
)

if (file.exists(cdc_graphic)) {
  knitr::include_graphics(cdc_graphic)
} else {
  cat(
    "Run `source(\"98_run_cdc_context.R\")` to create the optional ",
    "CDC context graphic."
  )
}
```

## Sources and methodology

Plumbing estimates come from U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey
table B25047, using the `r params$data_year - 4`–`r params$data_year`
five-year estimates. Disease context comes from the CDC National Notifiable
Diseases Surveillance System weekly tables and remains provisional.
